slices.focus: Tasha encounters older rescue cats at a neighborhood festival and begins seriously considering adoption
slices.summary: At a neighborhood fall festival, Tasha stops at a rescue adoption table and finds herself drawn to older, calm cats — especially a big orange cat that leans into the volunteer's hand. For the first time, the idea of adopting a cat moves from abstract fantasy to specific possibility. The volunteer's honest descriptions of temperament, health quirks, and lifestyle fit help Tasha evaluate practically rather than sentimentally. The agent helps her develop a four-point readiness checklist (weekly routine, budget with vet cushion, backup person, honesty about work chaos tolerance) and encourages treating the brochure on her counter as an observation prompt rather than a countdown clock. Tasha recognizes she is not ready yet but now knows the shape of 'yes' would be an older cat.
open_loops: Four-point readiness checklist — defined but not formally written
Observe home rhythms (sunny spots, quiet rooms) — informally started
Think about backup care person — no candidate yet
decisions: Meeting the rescue animals made Tasha more serious about eventually adopting an older cat once her routines feel steadie
